title: Explore local Codex conversation history
summary: List, show, search, export, resolve exact persisted task metadata, or inspect content-free completed-turn activity for local Codex tasks through the documented App Server interface.
use_when: The user wants to inspect, query, search, or export Codex tasks stored on this machine.
Another local product needs typed user/assistant conversation history with stable source references.
Another local product needs exact persisted task metadata, including the recorded working directory, for one canonical machine-local thread reference.
A local product needs exact completed-turn message scope and content-free evidence of completed Codex file changes, including recovery from a missed hook event.
do_not_use_when: The request is to continue, mutate, archive, delete, or send a message to a live Codex task.
The request requires reasoning traces, tool payloads, approvals, or raw Codex storage.
The user wants a model to interpret the conversations rather than retrieve them.
outcome: A complete requested App Server view normalized to user and assistant text, an exact persisted task summary for a canonical machine-local thread reference, or an explicit completed-turn activity view containing message counts and stable completed-file-change references without paths or diffs.
effects: List, show, search, export, activity, and doctor launch a short-lived local Codex App Server in a private process group, read its state-database view, and terminate that launch's inherited descendants on exit.
An exact-summary library call returns persisted task metadata, including the recorded working directory, only to its local caller and does not change CLI or activity output.
Show, search, and export can write sensitive user and assistant transcript text to the caller's terminal or redirected output; activity writes only counts, timing/status, and stable references.
The explicit refresh command allows App Server to scan its own logs and repair its own metadata; no other command enables that behavior.
authority: Codex App Server owns task discovery, persisted-storage compatibility, pagination, metadata, and full-history availability.
Conversations owns filters, normalized user/assistant output, stable references, copied-item deduplication, and failure-on-incomplete behavior.
Observed runtime status belongs to the newly launched App Server process and is not machine-wide liveness authority.
success: Every requested active and archived page completes through App Server.
Full-history operations complete through turn pagination or the explicit legacy fallback without raw-storage access.

An exact summary lookup requires a matching stable host identity, finds the thread exactly once across active and archived state-database metadata, and returns its recorded working directory without loading turns.
JSON output excludes reasoning, tool, approval, command, file-path, diff, and internal item payloads.
Activity accepts only a completed turn with a completion timestamp, validates every counted file-change entry, and fails when a session hint resolves the turn in multiple lineage members.
The short-lived launch and its inherited descendants do not remain running after the operation.
failure_and_recovery: A protocol error, timeout, unreadable page, or unsupported full-history record fails the operation instead of returning an incomplete normal result.
Use `conversations doctor` to inspect the selected CLI and recorded-version mismatch before changing installations.
Run `conversations refresh` only when App Server metadata repair is intended.
privacy: Task titles, working directories, normalized transcript text, stable activity references, and activity counts can be private.
The default macOS host reference is a one-way platform-identity hash; the raw hardware UUID is never exposed or retained, and an identity read failure stops the operation.
Conversations sends no transcript to a model or network service of its own, but redirected stdout becomes caller-owned retained data.
Interactive CLI calls inherit App Server stderr by default; privacy-sensitive embedded or scheduled callers must select the suppression policy when their logs cannot retain Codex diagnostics.

interfaces.label: Resolve exact task metadata from Rust

does_not_authorize: Reading Codex JSONL or SQLite storage directly.
Continuing, mutating, archiving, deleting, or messaging any Codex task.
Sending or publishing exported transcript text, or interpreting it with a model.

consumers.statement: A current-user caller or local Rust product may retrieve complete selected Codex task metadata, normalized user and assistant history, exact task summaries, or content-free completed-turn activity.
Task mutation, raw storage access, reasoning or tool-payload extraction, model interpretation, and machine-wide liveness monitoring are outside this capability.

preconditions.statement: The selected Codex binary can launch a compatible App Server and complete initialization, and any supplied host reference matches the client's stable current-machine identity.
Full-history and activity operations require App Server to return every requested page or the specifically documented method-unavailable legacy fallback.

inputs.statement: Inputs include the selected Codex binary and host identity, exact thread, turn, or session identifiers, archive and source-kind filters, cwd, title, updated-after, query text, limits, output mode, and diagnostic policy documented for the chosen interface.
Raw Codex file paths, SQLite queries, task mutations, arbitrary JSON-RPC methods, credential material, and private internal item kinds are not supported inputs.

outputs.statement: List and exact-summary reads return typed ThreadSummary metadata; show, search, and export return typed user-and-assistant-only normalized records with stable references.

Activity returns one completed turn's timing, status, user and assistant message counts, and stable references plus change counts for structurally valid completed nonempty file-change items, without bodies, paths, or diffs.
Refresh returns active and archived metadata counts after permitting App Server's own scan-and-repair path and never loads message content.

data_semantics.statement: The default corpus is active and archived interactive root tasks; subagents and exec tasks are included only by explicit independent filters, and copied fork items are deduplicated by item ID for snapshot, search, and export.
Only userMessage and agentMessage text become Message records; activity is a separate content-free projection, and observed runtimeStatus belongs only to the newly launched App Server.
Reasoning, images, commands, tool calls or results, approvals, file paths, diffs, raw storage records, and machine-wide task liveness are not corpus fields.

identity_and_units.statement: ThreadRef is host plus thread ID, TurnRef adds turn ID, and ItemRef adds item ID; exact summary requires one canonical host-matching ThreadRef to occur exactly once.
Message timestamps identify item, turn, or unknown precision; activity counts messages and completed change entries, and updated-after is Unix seconds.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Every requested active and archived metadata page and every selected full-history page must complete; protocol, page, timeout, ambiguity, or unsupported-record failure aborts instead of returning a normal partial corpus.
Ordinary operations read App Server's state-database-only view at invocation time; refresh is the sole operation that permits App Server metadata repair, and no Conversations cache is consulted.
The result does not guarantee that App Server metadata represents machine-wide live clients or that transcript state remains unchanged after the invocation.

access.statement: Conversations accesses Codex state only through one local documented App Server JSON-RPC session and writes results only to the caller's process output or typed library return.
It never opens Codex JSONL or SQLite storage, changes authentication, mutates tasks, sends transcript content to a model or network service of its own, or targets unrelated Codex processes.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: One invocation launches and initializes one App Server in a private process group, performs the bounded operation, terminates inherited descendants, reaps the direct child, and retains no Conversations state.
Full history prefers paginated thread/turns/list and uses legacy thread/read only for exact method-unavailable response; other errors never trigger fallback.
Activity validates exact thread first, searches session, parent, and fork lineage only on exact miss, and requires the requested turn to resolve to exactly one candidate.

operational_limits.statement: Activity reads newest-first pages of 100 until the requested turn; candidate and result limits bound supported list, search, and export work when supplied, while unbounded full-text work is proportional to every selected history.
Conversations offers no daemon, persistent index, event listener, background refresh, task mutation, raw-store fallback, or network API.
No App Server availability, wall-clock latency, corpus-size, throughput, or perpetual history-retention service-level objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 3 preserves the typed normalized schema, complete-read failure, explicit refresh, exact summary, activity separation, stable host references, and the narrow -32601 legacy fallback.
The selected Codex CLI and recorded task CLI versions may differ; doctor reports compatibility observations without converting them into machine-wide liveness.
No App Server protocol support window, future source-kind guarantee, or deprecation period for this capability version is promised.

reliances.statement: Every result relies on Codex App Server for task discovery, metadata, pagination, source records, storage compatibility, and availability, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes that exact data surface.
